title: Rock-and-roll dates and playing the Fender bass
summary: He recalls the Fender bass overpowering the upright on dates, his work on Flip Wilson and Carol Burnett, and a Frank De Vol call for all three basses.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Like, I've done some record dates that were pretty dumb here and there. But even then, you realize that no matter how dumb a thing is at the moment, it only lasts for a few hours. So you can live through anything. And I was in the beginning of I guess you'd call the Rock-and-Roll scene, and even when it would get so loud I couldn't stand it, I'd say to myself, "Well, in a couple of hours this will be over." Because that's what really did happen. When they first started using Fender basses on record dates, well, they used to double the Fender bass and the standup bass, and naturally, the Fender bass would wipe out everything the stand-up bass would do. Just like when I first started playing the bass, I remember the old-time drummers would do a press roll [RRRDDDRRRDDRRRP] through everything, which also swallowed up the bass sound. So...I don't know why I went back there, but...
Did you double on Fender bass?
Yeah, I play the Fender bass, too.
I didn't know that. I've never seen you with one.

Well, I own one, and I've... Well, I did The Flip Wilson Show, that was four years of Fender bass; and The Carol Burnett Show, I did some Fender bass on there. But I have to say that I was never in love with the Fender

bass. It's a very important instrument, I must say, because there are so many wonderful players. But after spending a lifetime trying to play the big bass, and you can't bow, you cannot play arco on a Fender bass... So I have no regrets. my son keeps my Fender bass most of the time. Last week, I had a picture call with Frank De Vol...

...and the contractor called and said, "Bring your Fender bass, tuba, and your stand-up bass." So they call the acoustic bass a "stand-up bass" now; that's how they designate between the two. So I took them all, and I got to play them all.
But my loves really are the tuba and the bass...or the bass and the tuba.
